label: STOPP D25: first-generation antihistamine for insomnia
title: Older antihistamine used for sleep
statement: First-generation antihistamines for insomnia (high risk of side-effects, Z-drugs safer and more appropriate for short-term use).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Older, sedating antihistamines such as doxylamine or promethazine are sometimes taken to help sleep, but they carry a high risk of confusion and drowsiness in older people.

medicine_groups.name: First-generation (older, sedating) antihistamines
medicine_groups.note: Count oral preparations, including tablets, capsules and liquids. Avomine contains promethazine teoclate. A Benadryl brand name alone does not identify the ingredient. Exclude creams and gels. Match hydroxyzine by ingredient name only. Trimeprazine is another name for alimemazine. Chlorpheniramine is another name for chlorphenamine. For combination products, check the exact product or the listed ingredients for chlorphenamine, triprolidine or brompheniramine. A range name such as Demazin, Dimetapp or Actifed, or the label Sleep Assist alone, does not identify the ingredient.

needs_facts.meets: Insomnia or trouble sleeping was a reason for using the antihistamine being checked.

options.words: Used for insomnia or trouble sleeping

rule_for_models: Before either finding, require a recorded age of at least 65 years. Below 65 there is no finding. If age is unknown, record eligibility as unresolved. Report a finding when the directions, a linked history entry or the pharmacist confirms that insomnia or trouble sleeping was a reason for the supplied Group A antihistamine. Cite the supply and the evidence of its purpose. If it was used only for another reason, such as allergy or nausea, or sleep use was ruled out, report no finding. Bedtime dosing or a diagnosis of insomnia alone leaves the reason uncertain. If the reason is missing or unknown, cite the supply, report a possible finding and name the missing fact "Reason for this antihistamine".
cannot_be_seen: Why the antihistamine was supplied and how it is really taken. A night-time direction suggests sleep but does not prove it. Also any sleep medicine bought over the counter or supplied by another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the antihistamine is still needed for sleep, whether a safer option for short-term sleep problems suits the person, and their risk of confusion, drowsiness and falls.
